patient_education_points: Some early changes can happen within 1 to 2 weeks, but clearer mood benefit often takes 4 to 6 weeks or longer.
Nausea, headache, sleep change, or restlessness may appear before mood benefit. Persistent or severe effects should be discussed with a clinician.
Sertraline is not considered addictive in the way alcohol, opioids, or benzodiazepines can be, but stopping suddenly can still cause uncomfortable discontinuation symptoms.
Do not stop suddenly without medical guidance. A clinician may recommend a gradual taper depending on dose, duration, and symptoms.
Alcohol can worsen sleepiness, mood symptoms, judgment, and medication tolerability.
Seek emergency help for overdose concerns, severe drowsiness, seizure, fainting, or dangerous behavior.
Recognise serotonin syndrome urgency signs: fever, confusion, sweating, agitation, tremor, or muscle rigidity.

animation_steps_and_mechanism_sequence.animation_subtitle: Sertraline blocks the serotonin transporter, leaving more serotonin available in the synaptic gap.
animation_steps_and_mechanism_sequence.toolbar_label: Animated synapse model (HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript)

visual_components.role: Presynaptic neuron releasing serotonin; contains neuron-body and axon.
Synaptic cleft containing serotonin particles, the SERT transporter, and stage labels.
Postsynaptic neuron with dendrite, four receptors (receptor-a..d), and neuron-body.
Six serotonin molecules animated across the cleft via the `serotoninFlow` keyframes.
Serotonin transporter shown as blocked (crossed-out indicator `.transporter i`) — visually conveys reuptake inhibition.
visual_components.marker: Rose/red box labelled 'SERT' with a diagonal crossed bar

visual_components.role: Four receptors on the receiving neuron that glow to indicate active serotonin signalling.

serotoninFlow.description: Serotonin particles drift left->right across the cleft, scaling up at ~45% then settling toward the postsynaptic side.

receptorGlow.description: Postsynaptic receptors pulse/scale and intensify their cyan glow to depict receptor activation.

miniSignal.description: Small serotonin signals travel left->right in the hero preview card.

mechanism_sequence_intended: 1. Serotonin is released from the sending (presynaptic) neuron into the synaptic gap.
2. Serotonin particles flow across the cleft toward postsynaptic receptors.
3. The SERT transporter (which would normally reuptake serotonin back into the presynaptic neuron) is BLOCKED by sertraline.
4. With reuptake blocked, more serotonin remains in the synaptic gap.
5. Postsynaptic receptors receive stronger/prolonged serotonergic signalling (depicted by the glowing receptors).
6. Over weeks, downstream adaptive changes produce the clinical mood/anxiety benefit seen in the timeline section.
